text:
lara-privacy: Heads-up: DSAR received for user anna+trial@example.com. There's a current retention-exception tagged LEG-INV-58 that covers some chat transcripts. We need to erase everything else (embeddings, telemetry, dev snapshots) and produce auditable receipts. Who can help map the safe path? :mag_right:

nate-sre: Which stores are definitely in-scope? vectordb, logs in s3, any Hive/warehouse exports?

lara-privacy: vectordb (managed), request logs in s3 (logs-prod-eu), and two debug snapshots in snapshot-store-eu (created during incident capture). No warehouse exports for this user as far as I can see.

teo-engr: Snapshot IDs? If they're in snapshot-store-eu and encrypted with ks-prod-eu-11, we'll need to coordinate with keystore team. Rotated keys could complicate proof that object is unrecoverable after deletion.

lara-privacy: Snapshots: snap-eu-20260111-0453 and snap-eu-20260202-1530. Keystore: ks-prod-eu-11. Legal says transcripts with LEG-INV-58 stay under hold; everything else must be purged per DSAR.

jamie-security: Ok two parallel tracks: 1) scoped erasure for non-held objects, 2) create signed receipts and ship them to compliance immutably. For RBAC: privacy worker needs vectordb:delete-documents, s3:DeleteObject, kms:Decrypt (to confirm key id used). This must be timebound and tenant restricted.

nate-sre: We can create a role `erasure-temp-LEG58-anna` with conditions: tenant_id=anna-tenant and expiration=6h. I prefer 6h vs 24h for blast radius. Any objections?

jamie-security: 6h is fine. Require MFA and run-as-service-account bound to the privacy-service identity. All actions must emit audit records with the following fields: actor, service_account, action, resource, key_fingerprint, trace_id, timestamp, verification-hash.

legal-bot: Legal confirms: transcripts under LEG-INV-58 remain; legal will release specific snapshot IDs after receipts are validated. We'll not sign off on deleting any snapshot listed in the hold until release email arrives.

teo-engr: There's an outstanding bug (TICKET-9402) where the async delete retry path can requeue doc ids if the KV rewrap fails silently. If we run mass deletes now, we must run a post-erase eviction and index-snapshot prune to avoid resurrection. I will attach the mitigation patch to the ticket.

nate-sre: Proposed plan: 1) create the scoped role, 2) run a small dry-run erasure that emits receipts but doesn't actually delete to validate receipt pipeline, 3) run real erasure during maintenance window, 4) trigger eviction + prune + verification scan. Agree?

lara-privacy: Sounds good. Dry-run first please — we need to show Legal the receipt format before they release snapshots.

jamie-security: Receipt format draft: newline-delimited key=value pairs (no nested JSON), fields: actor=, service_account=, action=, resource=, key_id=, timestamp=, trace_id=, hash=, signature=. We'll sign with HSM using org signing key. Store receipts in compliance-bucket/completed-dsars/LEG-INV-58/ and mark as immutable.

legal-bot: That format is acceptable. Please ensure verification hash uses SHA256 over canonicalized resource list + timestamp + trace_id. We'll require signed receipts for any snapshot release.

teo-engr: Implementation detail: vectordb delete API returns a tx_id; we should include tx_id in resource= or hash input. Also include a short blob of metadata: original_object_size and encryption_algorithm. We can flatten that into keys like orig_size and enc_alg in the ND key=value receipt. Avoid nested structures.

jamie-security: Good. Also ensure CLI and helper scripts do not write key metadata to /tmp in plaintext without wiping. Use in-memory temp files or write to an ephemeral mount that we zero and unmount.

lara-privacy: Here's the internal hud snippet I plan to run in dry-run mode (replace with real delete in step 3):
```bash
# list affected ids
redwood-privacy-cli list-ids --tenant anna-tenant --filter email:anna+trial@example.com > ids.txt
# dry-run delete (returns tx ids but does not remove)
redwood-privacy-cli delete --tenant anna-tenant --ids-file ids.txt --dry-run --trace dsar-4142201111 | tee dryrun-output.json
# capture keystore metadata (write directly to compliance bucket path)
redwood-keystore-cli describe --id ks-prod-eu-11 --json | redwood-storage-cli put --bucket compliance-bucket --key dsar/4142201111/key-meta.json
```

nate-sre: One nit: don't pipe keystore output through an unencrypted intermediate. redwood-storage-cli has an --encrypt-at-rest flag; use that. Also ensure the put operation uses server-side immutability lock.

jamie-security: I'll add an audit-forwarder hook to capture the delete API call and attach keystore key fingerprint. The forwarder will generate the verification-hash and call HSM-signer endpoint with the ND payload. HSM returns signature that we append as signature=. The forwarder will then write the signed receipt to compliance-bucket and emit an audit event.

teo-engr: Post-delete steps: run eviction service: /internal/evict --tenant anna-tenant --trace dsar-4142201111 and then run snapshot-prune tool: snapshotctl prune --tenant anna-tenant --retain-held SNAP_IDS. I'll schedule both after erasure. Also will run the TICKET-9402 patch in canary prior to mass run to reduce risk.

lara-privacy: Who will request the role creation? Nate?

nate-sre: I'll request `erasure-temp-LEG58-anna` with 6h expiry, scope tenant=anna-tenant, allowed_actions=[vectordb:DeleteDocument,s3:DeleteObject,kms:Decrypt] and require mfa. ETA 20m. I'll post the request id here once done.

jamie-security: Also add a policy condition to require `trace_id` in all delete calls and reject calls without it. That makes receipts harder to falsify.

teo-engr: For verification scan, I'll run a string-search across vectordb metadata and s3 object keys for substrings of the email and any known embeddings hashes. If anything returns, we escalate. We'll keep a binary pass/fail in the receipt metadata: verification=PASS/FAIL. If FAIL, we mark incident and run vuln triage.

lara-privacy: Legal note: after dry-run, we'll ask legal to pre-approve release template conditionally; once we give them the signed sample receipts, they can fast-track final release.

ops-bot: Maintenance window available: 2026-11-13T02:00Z-04:00Z. Confirm to lock window.

nate-sre: Locking window now. I'll attach request id ROLE-2026-ERASE-011 once created.

jamie-security: Reminder: keystore integrity check after deletion. Run a non-destructive decrypt attempt for a subset of snapshot ciphertexts to assert decryption fails for removed objects (where appropriate). If decryption succeeds unexpectedly, escalate immediately and preserve evidence.

teo-engr: Understood. We'll run key-rotation-history check: redwood-keystore-cli history --id ks-prod-eu-11 and compare encrypt/decrypt epochs. Include a short report in the receipts folder. Keep report as ND key=value lines to remain compatible.

lara-privacy: Thanks all. I'll update the DSAR ticket with plan and dry-run schedule. Please link TICKET-9402 and ROLE-2026-ERASE-011 in the ticket comments. I'll post back when legal gives conditional release. :raised_hands:
